drivingQuestion: Why does the mishna not teach the case 'this field was yours and I bought it from you'?
outcomeNote: The unit ends on the difficulty; its answer lies in the next unit.

segments.he: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בְּאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ כּוּ׳. וְלִיתְנֵי: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בְּאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ שָׂדֶה זוֹ שֶׁלְּךָ הָיְתָה, וּלְקַחְתִּיהָ מִמְּךָ?
segments.en: The mishna continues: «And Rabbi Yehoshua concedes in» a case where «one says to another:» This field belonged to your father, and I purchased it from him, that he is deemed credible. The Gemara asks: «And let» the mishna «teach: Rabbi Yehoshua concedes in» a case where «one says to another: This field belonged to you, and I purchased it from you.»
